title: Configuring the Development Terminal knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the central idea of “Configuring the Development Terminal”?
options: Ignore the actual output and infer success from a command returning without a visible error.
Explain command prompt and powershell considerations, then verify the expected behavior in a small, controlled Docker lab.
Assume one successful command proves security, persistence, and production readiness.
Change global daemon settings before establishing a baseline or reading the documentation.
questions.answer_key: Explain command prompt and powershell considerations, then verify the expected behavior in a small, controlled Docker lab.
questions.explanation: This lesson covers configuring the development terminal and the related syllabus points. Learners should describe the relevant concept, make a prediction, and verify it rather than rely on an untested assumption.

questions.prompt: For a lab covering configuring the development terminal, what is the strongest evidence of learning?
options: Record the command or configuration, predicted result, observed evidence, and one relevant edge case.
Assume the command is portable and skip reading its output.
Make several unrelated changes before collecting a baseline.
Use a production host so the result looks realistic.
questions.answer_key: Record the command or configuration, predicted result, observed evidence, and one relevant edge case.
questions.explanation: A useful lab connects a predicted result to actual output and checks an edge case. This is safer and more reproducible than assuming success.

questions.prompt: If an example related to configuring the development terminal fails, which response is best?
options: Delete every stopped container and unused volume before investigating.
Disable permissions or security controls until the example works.
Trust the image tag without inspecting the image or version.
Reproduce the issue, inspect state/logs/configuration, test one hypothesis at a time, and verify the fix.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the issue, inspect state/logs/configuration, test one hypothesis at a time, and verify the fix.
questions.explanation: The evidence-led approach keeps the diagnosis reproducible and avoids hiding the cause. For configuring the development terminal, verify the fix with the exact setting or command that failed.
